subject: POC charter + acceptance criteria — multilingual checkout assistant
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@lingoshop.com>, Tom Hsu <cto@lingoshop.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC charter + acceptance criteria — multilingual checkout assistant

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete POC proposal so we can lock timeline and owners.

Goal (what success looks like)
- Launch a 3-week trial that proves the checkout assistant can:
  - Correctly handle product/price/availability questions across US, ES, FR markets
  - Resolve 6 common cart-intent flows (apply discount, change shipping, saved payment) with high precision and low latency
- Outcome for LingoShop: >85% automation on targeted flows and clear handoff points for CS.

Proposed POC scope and timeline (3 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep, 2 business days): data & access, sample prompts, test harness + SOW sign (attached stub).
- Week 1 (integration): API keys, sample dataset ingestion, quick warm-up with 1k queries.
- Week 2 (evaluation): run evaluation suite for intent accuracy, slot extraction, response quality; tune prompts/temperature.
- Week 3 (acceptance & cutover): acceptance run, latency/load checks, canary deployment to 5% of real traffic.

Model recommendations (trial roster)
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (balanced: high instruction-following and good multilingual baseline).
- Fallback (low-latency / cost): Llama-2-7B (quantized) — used for fast short-turn queries and degraded mode.
- Multilingual specialist (for Spanish/French nuance): RedPajama-Chat-Multi-7B (prompt-tuned for EU locales).

Evaluation & acceptance criteria (examples to agree on)
- Intent classification: micro-F1 >= 0.88 on annotated holdout (ES/FR/EN combined).
- Slot extraction / entity precision >= 0.92 for payment/shipping entities.
- Generation quality: manual sample audit (n=100) with <= 8% critical hallucinations.
- Latency: 95th percentile token turnaround < 250ms for single-shot generation (EU region target).
- Stability: failure/retry rate < 1% under 50rps load.

Ownership
- Redwood: technical integration, model hosting, KPIs instrumentation (Karthik + Aditya).
- LingoShop: dataset labeling for holdout (Sarah), decision lead for acceptance (Tom).

Compliance & deployment notes
- You asked about data residency — for EU traffic we recommend Private deployment (VPC) with EU region routing; we can scope that in the SOW.
- We will only use sample logs for evaluation; production logs can be retained per your policy (we'll follow whichever retention you choose).

Attachments: LS-POC-SOW-v1.pdf (SOW + high-level pricing), lingoshop-sample-prompt-set.xlsx (example prompts + test cases).

Next steps / asks
1) Please confirm: 3-week trial length and acceptance criteria above (or note changes).
2) Can your procurement/ops review the attached SOW? If so, who should I loop in?
3) If you want us to prioritize EU VPC in the trial, say so and we’ll include a scoped private endpoint.

I'll book a 30-min kickoff for Thursday if that works — cc'ing Aditya for engineering availability.

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: LS-POC-SOW-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 122KB)]

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@lingoshop.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <cto@lingoshop.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC charter + acceptance criteria — multilingual checkout assistant

Thanks Karthik — the plan looks sensible. A few clarifications before we lock: 

1) EU focus: primary test will be ES / FR markets (we’ll also include US for baseline). EU data must not leave our EU tenancy during the trial — is a VPC endpoint a hard requirement for that?
2) Acceptance metrics: the intent F1 target looks right; for generation quality we prefer a labelled false-positive definition (i.e., giving incorrect pricing or policy statements = critical). Can you propose an audit rubric?
3) Procurement: I’m looping Tom (CTO) — procurement will want a one-page SOW summary + an estimate for a potential 3-month pilot (we may expand).

Budget: tight — if the POC demonstrates the automation targets we'll look at a reserved capacity pilot. Any flexibility on a short-term promo for startups/partners?

Also, could you confirm the model roster you plan to test? We have in-house LLM infra but prefer Redwood to host the trial.

Best,
Sarah
Product Lead — Conversational Commerce
LingoShop

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@lingoshop.com>, Tom Hsu <cto@lingoshop.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC charter + acceptance criteria — multilingual checkout assistant

Sarah — great questions, answered inline and added a compact audit rubric below.

EU residency: yes — we can provision a Private endpoint (EU region) for the trial so logs and inference requests are routed and stored in your EU tenancy. That will add a modest setup lead time (2–3 business days) and a small one-time infra setup fee; we’ll call that out in an SOW addendum.

Audit rubric (sample)
- Critical error: any generated response that returns incorrect pricing, discloses PII, or gives actionable but wrong checkout steps. Fail if >8/100 critical errors.
- Major error: incorrect slot extraction leading to wrong flow but recoverable after clarification. Fail threshold >12/100.
- Minor: phrasing issues, polite tone mismatches, or missing small non-critical attributes. Expect these but not included in hard fail.

Model roster — more detail
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (primary): select for best instruction-following + general multilingual capabilities. We'll run with temperature 0.0–0.2 for deterministic slot extraction and structured outputs.
- Llama-2-7B-quant (fallback): cheap, fast; used for latency-sensitive quick replies (simple confirmations, presence checks).
- RedPajama-Chat-Multi-7B: used only for ES/FR heavy queries in second half of Week 2 if we see degradation on locale-specific utterances.

Evaluation plan (metrics + how we measure)
- We’ll create a labeled test set (n≈1,200 queries: 400 EN / 400 ES / 400 FR). LingoShop provides 150 labelled queries per locale; Redwood will augment and label the rest.
- Intent & slot metrics computed automatically from the structured output.
- Manual audit: 100 sampled responses per locale evaluated by LingoShop SME against rubric.
- Load & latency: synthetic replay at 30rps + 95th pctl metrics measured in EU endpoint.

Commercial asks you flagged
- Promo: we can extend a one-time 20% credit on hosted usage for the POC (applies to first-month invoices) — subject to signature on SOW.
- For a 3-month reserved pilot we can discuss tiered discounts; we’ll include price bands in the SOW.

Next steps I’ll action by EOD:
- Update the SOW with EU VPC option and a one-page summary for procurement (attached as SOW v1).
- Draft the labeled test-set template and send to Sarah for initial 150 sample queries.
- Book kickoff with Aditya, myself and your engineering lead — propose Thu 21st 09:00-09:30 PT.

Regards,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Sarah — thanks for the clarity. We’re aligned on scope and EU VPC requirement — please include the VPC addendum in the SOW. Quick additional asks from infra:
- Temporary trial license with ability to route only EU requests to the EU endpoint (no cross-region fallbacks unless explicitly configured).
- Can Redwood provide a short support window during the integration (Mon–Fri 8:00–17:00 CET) for the first two weeks?

Commercial note: the 20% credit sounds fine for the POC. For a 3-month pilot we’ll need more concrete SLAs on latency and an uplifted credit model. We’ll review the SOW and get procurement back to you by Mon.

I’ll be on the kickoff. Please add Aditya as the Redwood engineer contact for technical items.

Tom Hsu
CTO, LingoShop
